author: andrew-k-park
title: Windows CC build fails with linker out-of-memory error LNK1102 under high parallelism
signature: Windows Release build runs out of memory - compiler fatal error C1060 (out of heap space) and linker fatal error LNK1102 (out of memory) under high parallelism|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: Build_And_Run_Collect_Mode
failed_jobs.symptom: Ninja/MSVC link step for ov_subgraphs_dumper_tests.exe and ov_ir_frontend_tests.exe failed with LNK1102 fatal error: out of memory

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_windows_cc
failed_jobs.symptom: Downstream status-check gate job failed solely because Build_And_Run_Collect_Mode failed; not an independent failure

root_cause: The Windows Conditional Compilation (Collect Mode) build uses CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL: 31, launching many parallel MSVC link.exe processes concurrently on the Windows runner. Under this level of parallelism, the linker for ov_subgraphs_dumper_tests.exe and ov_ir_frontend_tests.exe exhausts available memory and fails with LNK1102, aborting the ninja build. This is the 18th recorded occurrence of this exact signature on this workflow since 2026-11-03, indicating a persistent, known capacity/parallelism issue with the Windows CC runner rather than a defect introduced by the triggering commit/PR (#40003, a GPU-plugin GroupedMatMul fix unrelated to Windows linking).
reproduction_steps: Not directly reproducible outside CI without a similarly memory-constrained Windows runner. Locally: configure with CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL=31 (or similarly high) and CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release on a machine with limited RAM, then run `ninja` to build the collect-mode target set; link-time OOM (LNK1102) reproduces when too many link.exe processes run concurrently.
recommended_actions: Reduce CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL for the Windows CC Collect Mode job, or split link-heavy test targets into separate batches to lower peak concurrent linker memory usage.

Consider adding /INCREMENTAL:NO already present, but also enable linker throttling (e.g., limit parallel link jobs via Ninja pool definitions) so compile and link phases do not compete unbounded for memory.
Evaluate moving this job to a Windows runner with more RAM, given 18 recurrences of the same OOM signature in 3 weeks.
File a tracking issue referencing this recurring pattern (signature_hash 80cfa127185fbf3e) so CI infra owners can prioritize a durable fix rather than relying on reruns.
prevention_strategies: Cap Ninja's link-job concurrency independently from compile-job concurrency (Ninja `pool` with depth limit) on memory-constrained Windows runners, and monitor peak memory during CC builds to catch regressions in parallelism settings before they cause OOM linker failures.
historical_context: This exact signature (Windows Release build linker/compiler OOM, LNK1102/C1060) has recurred 18 times between 2026-11-03 and this run (2026-11-23), consistently on this same Windows Conditional Compilation workflow, unrelated to the specific commit/PR that happened to trigger each run. It is a known, unresolved infrastructure capacity issue.
